description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. GOI expanded the National Industrial Corridor Development Program of India by including 6 additional corridors to the existing 5 corridors and expanded the institutional mandate of NICDCL as national program development agency and knowledge partner of NICDIT.

1.2. Skill Development Training programs developed jointly by NICDCL and NSDC to upgrade skills of local labor force within the industrial corridors in line with industry demand with focus on female labor.

1.3. The government launched the PM Gati Shakti (GS, Speed for Economic Strength) National Master Plan and integrated National Industrial Corridor Development Program (NICDP) into the GS plan, and SPVs commence its implementation by allocating 40% of already-acquired and developed land at industrial nodes for establishment of factories, industrial plants, and common and social infrastructures following granting of environmental clearances.

1.4. To ensure inclusive representation and efficient institutional coordination between the center and the states for industrial corridor development, the Government (i) appointed female directors in SPV boards of all operational NICDP SPVs, and (ii) established four new special purpose vehicles (SPVs) ($1.09 billion in node infrastructure investment) including both central and state government officials on the Board of SPVs.

1.5. To upgrade the skills of labor force in industrial nodes, NICDCL (i) approved “Skill India” curriculum focused on gender inclusivity through various programs tailored for women and (ii) commenced its implementation in at least 3 industrial corridor nodes, with at least 50% of women employees from firms participating in the training programs.

2.1. NICDIT's board approved the following documents to streamline the approval and oversight process of development of industrial corridors: (i) a detailed Investment and Financing Plan for NICDIT which will include modalities and readiness criteria for disbursement to SPVs. (ii) guidelines on criteria on appraisal, preparation, and prioritization of all SPV project proposals to ensure consistency and uniformity in corridor development.

2.2. NICDCL developed guidelines on gender inclusive transport including infrastructure initiatives and Services and Policy initiatives in and around nodes and adopted by an SPV as identified by NICDCL.

2.3. NICDIT's board has approved a green industrial corridor development policy framework that addresses sustainable planning, and development of climate resilient infrastructure within industrial corridors.

2.4. To enable financing of industrial corridor projects, (i) NICDCL approved a strategy to leverage equity and raise alternative sources of finance for future expansion of NICDIT approved projects, (ii) 3 SPV Boards commenced implementation for financing the development of infrastructure projects in accordance with the strategy.

2.5. To increase investment in corridor areas (i) NICDIT implemented the new appraisal and financing mechanism by appraising at least 5 new proposals from the states for development of industrial nodes, located outside of environmentally important areas, and in line with NICDP standards and requirements and (ii) NICDCL approved a model concession agreement for adoption by all NICDP SPVs for consistent operationalization of utility companies in NICDP nodes.

2.6. To improve workplace safety, security, and convenience for female labor force, (i) at least 3 NICDCL-approved projects implemented guidelines on gender inclusive industrial housing for employees, including gender related provisions; and (ii) NICDCL approved and implemented HR process manuals for the node SPVs which include gender-inclusive measures like workplace safety, and equal opportunity.

2.7. To promote environmental sustainability and climate resilience, Government adopted green industrial corridor development policy (GICDP) framework in at least three NICDP industrial nodes and applied the objectives of the GICDP in the master plans of new industrial node development.

3.1. DPIIT established a national single window clearance system platform for one-stop digital national portal, that integrates the existing clearance systems of various ministries/departments of GOI and will have a single, unified application form for the investors.

3.2. NICDCL issued Instructions to all nodes to make available industrial infrastructure and land related information in IILB portal of DPIIT—that addresses transparency and ease of availability of information for the investors.

3.3. NICDCL formulated a marketing plan and communicated to SPVs to facilitate private sector investment including in social and infrastructure projects that includes: (i) market extension program to attract private sector investment in potential opportunities; and (ii) Awareness building on digital platforms to share potential investment information.

3.4. DPIIT launched an upgraded IPRS, a digital platform, to (i) enhance transparency of information for investors in making selections on investment locations; and (ii) promote competition among Industrial Park owners/states to improve physical infrastructure as well as ease regulatory barriers.

3.5. NICDCL board approved guidelines on skills upgrading and training relevant for employment to nodes within industrial corridors to skill local labor force in industrial areas, based on a gender sensitive needs assessment and available market opportunities.

3.6. To synchronize central and state single window clearance systems, 11 industrial corridor states developed and integrated single window clearance system platform with government of India's national single window clearance mechanism.

3.7. To promote ease of doing business for investors, Government through DPIIT (i) reduced compliance costs on businesses and citizens digitizing 1,200 processes, (ii) completed gap assessment of industrial parks in at least 14 industrial corridor states covered under NICDP and (iii) adopted its recommendations in the implementation of financing plan for industrial parks.

3.8. To improve attractiveness of industrial corridors for business, NICDCL (i) provided the land data of all NICDP industrial nodes through NICDCL portal; (ii) connected investors to the nodal officers of the SPVs to facilitate private investment; (iii) implemented an investor outreach program in all NICDP industrial nodes; and (iv) published sex disaggregated data on employment of labor force in NICDP industrial nodes on NICDL portal.
